Ella Langley's "Choosin' Texas" made an estimated $32.0K on Spotify in the US in one week. The label kept about $20.5K. 💸

The song did 8,001,246 US Spotify streams in the week of Oct 8, 2026, #3 on the US chart after 51 weeks (461.5M total chart streams, via kworb). It's the lead single from Dandelion, released Oct 17, 2025 on SAWGOD/Columbia, and it hit #1 on the Billboard Hot 100.

At an estimated $0.004 per stream, about 80% of the payout goes to the recording. On a typical major-label deal the artist royalty is about 20% of that before recoupment: roughly $5.1K for Langley as artist. Publishing (the other ~20%) goes to four credited writers, Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert, Luke Dick and Joybeth Taylor, about $1.6K each. Lambert, Langley and Ben West produced it.

Add it up: about $6.7K a week for Langley (artist + writer) vs $20.5K for the label, about 3x. Over 51 weeks of US chart streams that's an estimated $1.85M in total.

Fair split, or should the artist get more? 👇

Data: Spotify US weekly chart via kworb.net, credits via Wikipedia/Billboard; payout figures are estimates · as of Oct 8, 2026 chart week
